page: Microsoft Azure M832ids_16_v3 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine from the Mids High Memory v3 series, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, providing 832 dedicated vCPUs alongside 15,200 GB of system memory. This configuration yields approximately 18.27 GB of RAM per vCPU, establishing an extreme-tier memory profile designed for monolithic workloads requiring massive shared memory space.

The server includes 429 GB of local SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent managed disk attachments. It includes no hardware GPU accelerators and assigns zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Tenancy is isolated, ensuring dedicated access to underlying physical server hardware without interference from multi-tenant hypervisor neighbors.

Deploying this scale of instance prioritizes deep resource consolidation over horizontal scaling. The primary trade-off is the relatively compact 429 GB local SSD relative to the 15.2 TB memory capacity, requiring external storage architectures for data-heavy persistence. It is engineered primarily for large-scale enterprise in-memory databases like SAP HANA, extreme OLTP engines, and complex data-warehouse aggregation.
description: Microsoft Azure M832ids_16_v3 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance from the Mids High Memory v3 family on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. Built on x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the machine features 832 dedicated vCPUs and 15,200 GB of total RAM, delivering approximately 18.27 GB of memory per core. The server configuration includes 429 GB of local SSD storage, supports Premium Storage tiers, and contains no GPU accelerators. The isolated execution environment guarantees dedicated physical hardware to prevent tenant contention. Given its high core count and large memory-to-core ratio, this server is oriented toward enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive relational database workloads, and compute-heavy analytics that require large unified memory pools rather than distributed nodes.
